sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emuley, I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Cure Body.
Cure Body is a small island country
in the Pacific Ocean.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Cure Body?
Cure Body is in the central Pacific Ocean.
It is made of 33 small islands.
These islands are in three groups.
The Gilbert Islands, the Phoenix Islands, the Line Islands.
Some islands are far apart.
The country is very spread out.
What is the capital of Cure Body?
The capital city is South Tarawa.
It is in the Gilbert Islands Group.
South Tarawa is a narrow island, but many people live there.
There are also villages and small towns on other islands.
How many people live in Cure Body?
About 120,000 people live in Cure Body.
Most people live on the main island, Tarawa.
The people are called I Cure Body, say E-Kiribas.
They are known for being friendly, respectful,
and close to nature.
What language do people speak in Cure Body?
The two official languages are Cure Body,
also called Gilbertis, English.
People use Cure Body in daily life.
English is used in schools and for official things.
What is the weather like in Cure Body?
Cure Body has a hot and humid climate.
It is tropical and close to the equator.
There are two seasons, dry season from May to October.
Wet season from November to April.
It rains a lot during the wet season.
The temperature is warm all year.
What does Cure Body look like?
Cure Body has flat islands with white sand,
coconut trees and blue lagoons, coral reefs and clear water.
There are no mountains or rivers.
The land is very low and climate change
is a big problem for Cure Body.
What animals live in Cure Body?
Cure Body is home to sea birds, like forget birds and turns.
Fish, crabs, and sea turtles.
Coconut crabs, big and strong.
Reef animals, like coral, starfish, and eels.
There are no large land animals.
What do people eat in Cure Body?
Food in Cure Body is simple, local, and fresh.
People eat fish, grilled, boiled, or dried.
Rice and bread fruit.
Coconut in many forms.
Milk, oil, or raw.
Pandan is fruit and tarot.
Sometimes people also eat chicken or imported food.
What do people drink in Cure Body?
People drink coconut water, natural and refreshing.
Rainwater, collected in tanks.
Imported drinks, like tea or juice.
Toddy, a sweet drink from coconut trees.
Clean drinking water is very important in island life.
What is life like in Cure Body?
Life in Cure Body is simple, quiet, and community-based.
People enjoy fishing and swimming, talking with neighbors,
dancing and singing, going to church, spending time with family.
Many people live in traditional houses made from palm leaves and wood.
What are some holidays and traditions in Cure Body?
Independence Day, July 12th.
Christmas and Easter, with church and music.
National Culture Day, with dancing and storytelling.
Family Day, time to be together.
People wear colorful clothes, dance to wine,
traditional dance, and eat with family.
Some fun facts about Cure Body.
The name Cure Body is pronounced Cure Boss.
Cure Body is the first country to see the sun rise every day.
The flag shows the ocean, a sun, and a bird.
Most land is just 1 to 3 meters above sea level.
Cure Body may one day move because of rising seas.
Now you know many things about Cure Body.
You know where it is, what people speak, and how they live.
You learned about the islands, food, culture, and daily life.
Well done.
I am Mimi Lee.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Cure Body.
Tia Bo.
